title: Siyum
hook: finishing a tractate is celebrated with a meal
tomorrow: Maimonides wrote ten chapters on coming back. where do they start?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two voices on a finished book, and a Kaddish of a world made new: finished and begun. Today the voices stop arguing, and somebody sets the table.

Birthday cake. Pizza after the last game of the season. Somebody's grandmother pressing a plate into your hands at a graduation. When something big ends, people reach for food. So what's on the table when you finish a tractate? A meal. Bagels, cake, herring, whatever the community likes, set out after the last lines, the hadran and the Kaddish. It has a name, the seudat siyum, the meal of completion.
screen: `CAKE. PIZZA. A PLATE IN YOUR HANDS.` → `WHAT'S ON THE TABLE?` → `THE MEAL OF COMPLETION.`

segments.voice: Where does that meal come from? One root is a line in the Talmud, in tractate Shabbat. Abaye, a sage, says, in plain words: may I be rewarded, because whenever I saw a young scholar finish a tractate, I made a festive day for the rabbis. Notice whose finish it is. Not Abaye's own. A young student's. Abaye throws the party for someone else's accomplishment, and counts that as something worth a reward. So the siyum meal isn't a trophy for the one who finished. It's a table the whole community sits at, to say: this matters to all of us. Something to tell a friend tonight: there's a custom on the day before Passover, when firstborn sons traditionally fast, that a siyum is held that morning, and the meal of completion releases the people who join it from the fast. A finished book changes a fast day into a feast. And that's why the meal matters to the senses. You don't just know you finished. You taste it. Bread, salt, sweetness, voices at a crowded table. The learning was words on a page for weeks. At the end, it becomes something you can chew.
screen: `ABAYE: A FEAST FOR SOMEONE ELSE.` · `A TABLE FOR EVERYONE.` · `A FAST TURNED INTO A FEAST.` · `YOU TASTE THE FINISH.` · then, large: `YOU FINISHED A TRACTATE.`

segments.voice: Take one small thing to eat, something you like: a piece of fruit, a cracker, a bite of something sweet. Eat it slowly, noticing the taste, the texture, the smell. Let it stand for something you, or someone near you, finished lately.
screen: `ONE SMALL BITE.` · `TASTE. TEXTURE. SMELL.` · `FOR SOMETHING FINISHED.`

segments.voice: Siyum. Hebrew for completion: finishing a tractate, and the meal where everyone tastes it together.

howItsDone: A siyum ends with a festive meal, the seudat siyum, open to everyone present; on the day before Passover synagogues often hold a siyum so that firstborns may join the meal instead of fasting.
